manual_reviewer_note: Verified visually in the official §6-205 RA-4 dimensional schedule. The phrase explicitly identifies 200 ft. as the lot-width requirement measured at the house location. The separate 125 ft. figure belongs to an adjacent requirement and is not used as lot width.

The official §6-205 RA-4 schedule provides a maximum of 3-1/2 stories. A full-text search of the canonical PDF found no directly applicable RA-4 maximum-height value in feet and no operative stories-to-feet conversion rule; §6-204 (Exceptions to Maximum Height and Parking Space Requirements), which might have supplied one, is marked 'Deleted 6/11/86' on page 231. A feet-based value cannot be inferred.

The ordinance explicitly limits lot-coverage applicability to R-MF, R-6 three-family, and commercial zones (§6-5(34.1)). RA-4 is not included. Minimum Green Area (84% for RA-4, §6-205) remains auxiliary evidence and is not converted into maximum lot coverage, since §6-5(34.1)'s definition of Lot Coverage includes buildings, parking, driveways, decks, pools, patios, and terraces -- green area is not shown to be its legal complement.

§6-154 (Parking and Garages for Residential Purposes) is the controlling single-family residential parking provision for RA-4. It imposes a qualitative sufficiency requirement rather than a numeric minimum expressed as spaces per dwelling unit. Numeric parking schedules found elsewhere (§6-155: 1-1.6 spaces/bedroom for two-family/multi-family; §6-121: BMR units) apply to different uses and are not substituted for the RA-4 principal single-family rule.

Greenwich defines a multi-family dwelling (§6-5(19)) as a building containing three or more dwelling units. Multifamily housing is not among the enumerated RA-4 principal uses, and §6-93 expressly excludes all other principal uses. Therefore multifamily housing with three or more dwelling units is prohibited as a principal use in RA-4.

§6-99 expressly includes RA-4 among its named eligible zones (also for the 1,200 sq ft external-ADU size cap under RA-2/RA-4). A conforming ADU is allowed subject to objective standards (owner occupancy, size limits, lot/setback conformance, parking, utility/septic documentation) and staff-level Planning and Zoning Office / Town Planner or designee approval -- not Commission discretionary review. Special Permit / Commission review applies only to the exception case (oversized ADU or nonconforming lot per §6-99(3)(E)), not the ordinary conforming pathway.
